passages.note: Her committee testimony on her own bill describes a services-first sequence but names no penalty type, so it does not separate the enforcement-side rungs.
The snapshot reports authorship and summarizes the measure in the reporter's words; it does not print the bill's operative text, so provision_quote is null.

rows.reasoning: Carrasco authored Senate Bill 285, which the reporting describes as banning camping, sleeping or long-term sheltering on public land while requiring a warning and an offer of shelter and services first — the graduated-warning architecture of "Prohibiting encampments on public property, enforced through graduated warnings and civil penalties" combined with the criminal penalty of "Banning public camping and sleeping with criminal penalties to maintain public safety and order". In her own words the bill works "through a clear, multi-step process that prioritizes services before enforcement", so neither of those two rungs is matched clause for clause, and ruling out the first three rungs is not evidence for the one left. Neither snapshot prints the bill's operative text or Carrasco's own vote, so the surviving evidence establishes the enforcement side only.
